maya: Seeing a weird kernel-time spike in the small-batch path after the kernel-selection tweak we rolled yesterday. p95 token latency +30% on the KV-heavy traces :grimacing:
chris: thanks — can you share a quick nsys capture? prefer trace=cuda,nvtx,osrt so we get both kernel timeline and our NVTX batch markers.
sasha: fwiw small-batch often hits a different cuBLAS/cuBLASLt kernel or a custom attention kernel that regresses on short seqs. also KV evictions can add host-side stalls.
maya: putting a capture on now. quick Q: what CLI flags you want? i can do 30s or 60s.
perf-bot: Recommended baseline command (copy/paste):
```
nsys profile -o out/kernel_spike -t cuda,nvtx,osrt --duration=60 --capture-range=nvtx --capture-range-end=1 --sample=cpu
```
Note: we use NVTX capture ranges around the end-to-end request path so you don't record the whole system. --duration is wall time limit in seconds.
chris: couple notes: 1) for short bursts set duration >=30 to catch a few repetitions; 2) add `--sample=cpu` to catch any host sampling stalls; 3) if file gets huge, reduce trace categories to `cuda,nvtx` only.
sasha: also push NVTX ranges around the batching hot-loop. in Python: `nvtx.range_push("batch_start")` before the batch send, and `nvtx.range_pop()` after. this lets capture-range=nvtx focus exactly on request windows.
maya: doing `--duration=90` and will run twice: one with quantized kernels enabled (post-change) and one with the previous kernel selector.
perf-bot: Helpful analysis checklist after capture:
- open in Nsight Systems -> Kernel Timeline -> look for sudden long kernels labeled like `multi_head_attention` or `cublasLtMatmul`
- filter by CUDA API duration > 2ms to spot outliers
- inspect NVTX lanes to correlate when KV cache hits/evicts happen
- export timeline CSV and grep for large gaps on host side (ie: CPU waiting on device)
chris: if you see a pattern where short sequences trigger a FWD kernel that spends lots of time in shared-mem or reduces occupancy, that's a sign the kernel selector mis-picked tiling. compare CC and grid dims between runs.
sasha: also check kernel launch counts. a spike in small kernels (many launches) can kill perf via launch overhead. batching heuristics might be splitting into sub-batches unexpectedly.
maya: ran both captures, uploading now. preliminary look: the regressed run shows repeated ~2.4ms kernels labelled `attention_tile32` vs the baseline ~0.9ms `attention_tile64` for same seq len.
chris: aha — selector switched to tile32 for short seqs after fallback rule change. tile32 has lower occupancy at our GPU (A100) for these shapes. that explains 2.6x per-kernel time.
sasha: next steps:
- patch selector rules to prefer tile64 for seq<=128 for this model (temp revert)
- add an automated eval that samples short-seq latency after selector changes
- add an NVTX-based test harness to trigger the exact batch shapes to capture automatically with CI nsys runs (short, deterministic)
maya: agreed. i'll open a PR for selector patch and attach the nsys timeline + screenshot in the PR. thanks for the pointers :thumbsup:
perf-bot: quick tip for future captures: add `--output` with a unique name and compress (`nsys export --output out.sqlite --format=sqlite`) before sharing to keep the artifacts small.
chris: perfect — great triage team, feel free to ping me if the selector PR affects other models.
maya: will do, closing thread after PR lands.
